name: Ulthera DeepSEE

lead: DeepSEE is an Ulthera ultrasound system with built-in imaging, used by clinicians to tighten lax skin on the lower face and under the chin for a firmer jawline.

Microfocused ultrasound delivers heat at set depths below the skin surface, while imaging lets the operator see tissue layers and target them. A single-arm study of 201 participants for lower-face and submental laxity was registered and completed; its results were not available in the sources reviewed.

paras: It is performed by a trained clinician in an office session. Tightening builds over the following weeks to months, and it is used by people who want a non-surgical option for lower-face laxity.
Specific adverse-event data for this model were not available in the reviewed sources. MFU-V devices are discussed in the literature as noninvasive alternatives to surgery.

angle.text: DeepSEE is used for non-surgical tightening of the lower face and under-chin, aiming at a sharper jawline. Imaging-guided focused ultrasound heats tissue at set depths so the operator can target it. A 201-person study is registered.

lead: The Ulthera DeepSEE system is a microfocused ultrasound with visualization (MFU-V) device from Ulthera, used by clinicians for noninvasive tightening and lifting of the lower face and the area under the chin (submentum). It is used to give a firmer jawline and a lifted, more defined lower face without surgery [1][2].

MFU-V delivers focused ultrasound energy at set depths beneath the skin while real-time imaging lets the operator see tissue layers such as the SMAS, fat and dermis. A 2021 review describes heating to roughly 60 to 70 degrees C at points in the dermis and subdermis, an immediate collagen contraction, and then new collagen and elastin formation over about 48 hours to 10 weeks, with remodeling continuing for up to a year [1].

Published results for MFU-V in the broader literature, as summarised in that review, include a brow lift in 86% of patients at 90 days and a submental lift in about 73%. The review was written by MFU-V practitioners and funded by Merz Asia Pacific, which markets Ultherapy [1]. A registered, completed single-arm study of 201 participants evaluated the DeepSEE system for skin laxity of the lower face and submentum [2].

paras: MFU-V devices are described as a noninvasive alternative to surgery for facial and body skin laxity, alongside nonablative radiofrequency and laser-assisted technologies [1]. A consensus paper from Asian clinicians reviewed these technologies and proposed recommendations for optimizing MFU-V in Asian patients [1].

The review describes low-energy microfocused ultrasound delivered at depths of 1.5, 3.0 and 4.5 mm, creating microthermal coagulation points in the dermis and subdermis while sparing the overlying tissue. Real-time imaging to about 8 mm lets the clinician see the SMAS, subcutaneous fat, dermis and epidermis and avoid structures such as bone and vessels [1].

A registered trial (NCT04795622), started in March 2021 and listed as completed, enrolled 201 participants to evaluate the effectiveness and safety of the DeepSEE system for skin laxity in the lower face and submentum [2]. A separate 20-person trial of MFU-V at multiple depths is recruiting [3].

The 2021 consensus review summarised published MFU-V data: face and neck laxity improved in about 78% of patients with 67% sustained at 180 days, submental lift in about 73% with about 69% maintained at three months, and 80% clinical improvement at 90 days in one Asian lower face and neck study [1].

Results are described as lasting up to one to two years in some studies, with maintenance treatment generally suggested at 12 to 18 month intervals. The consensus authors advise using imaging to select depths for each patient and note that Asian patients often have denser SMAS and thinner skin, calling for customised treatment [1].

According to the review, adverse events are mainly linked to poor technique, including burns, blistering and scarring, and pain varies by patient and area. The authors caution about copycat devices lacking safety feedback and clinical validation [1]. Model-specific adverse-event data for DeepSEE were not located.

timeline.event: Study of the DeepSEE system for lower face and submentum laxity begins (NCT04795622) [2]; MFU-V consensus review published [1].
Trial of long-term MFU-V efficacy at multiple depths begins recruiting [3].
